The learned Advocate also submits that challenging the service of summons under Order V rule 17 and rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure the defendant-petitioner-appellants instituted their miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the petitioners specifically asserted that there was no service of summons notice upon them. The learned Advocate submits that under the ambit of law the onus of proof lies upon the plaintiff to prove that the summons were duly served upon the defendant-petitioners, but they have failed to discharge their onus of proof by any tangible evidence. The learned Advocate in support of his contention referred some decisions of our Apex Court reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162, 16 BLD(AD)4 and 9 MLR(AD)158 and two decisions of this Court reported in 25 DLR 91, and 1990 BLD 151.

It is a fact that, in the original suit the service of summons was allegedly done under Order V rule 17 and 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure and subsequent to that, the defendants challenging that service of notice; instituted the Miscellaneous Case being No.06 of 2006 before the learned trial court and in that case it was their pleading that in fact there was no service upon them and the serving officer in collusion with the plaintiff served the summons notice after hanging. In the instant nature of case limitation is no doubt immaterial if it is proved that in fact there is no service of summons upon the defendants. The burden of proof in the instant case lies upon the plaintiffs to prove that in fact the service was done and the defendants suppressing the facts of , service of notice upon then raised their plea on non-service of summons. In the instant case; as I have come across from the relevant papers on records that the plaintiff have hopelessly failed to discharge his onus of proof that the summons notice in fact was duly served upon the defendant under Order V rule 17 and 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Neither the concerned process-server nor the witness in presence of whom the alleged service was done, was examined by the learned court below before arrival  at a decision that in fact there was service of summons upon the defendant-petitioners. It is required to be mentioned here that, due to distinguishable character the decision cited by Mr. Ranjan Kumar Chakrovorty is not applicable in this instant case.
